  html:

> Status: draft. This is exploratory research code, not a clinical prediction tool.

Input: sample-level expression, patient-level outcomes, and a patient-grouped
train/test split. Choose features and the probability threshold using training
data before evaluating held-out patients.

## 1. Load sample labels and expression

The expression CSV has one row per feature and one column per sample. The split
TSV has one row per sample and columns `sample_id`, `patient_id`, `outcome`,
and `split`; `split` is `train` or `test`. All samples from one patient must
have the same outcome and stay in one split.

```{r}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(tidymodels)
library(brglm2)
library(ggplot2)
library(qs2)

expression <- readr::read_csv("input/feature_expression.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
splits <- readr::read_tsv("input/train_test_split.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE)
stopifnot("feature_id" %in% names(expression))
stopifnot(all(c("sample_id", "patient_id", "outcome", "split") %in% names(splits)))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(expression$feature_id), !anyDuplicated(splits$sample_id))
stopifnot(!anyNA(splits$patient_id), all(splits$split %in% c("train", "test")))
train_patients <- unique(splits$patient_id[splits$split == "train"])
test_patients <- unique(splits$patient_id[splits$split == "test"])
stopifnot(length(intersect(train_patients, test_patients)) == 0)

expression_matrix <- expression |>
  tibble::column_to_rownames("feature_id") |>
  as.matrix()
stopifnot(is.numeric(expression_matrix), all(is.finite(expression_matrix)))
model_data <- as.data.frame(t(expression_matrix)) |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("sample_id") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(splits, by = "sample_id")
stopifnot(nrow(model_data) == nrow(splits), !anyNA(model_data$outcome))
stopifnot(all(vapply(
  split(as.character(model_data$outcome), model_data$patient_id),
  function(x) length(unique(x)) == 1L,
  logical(1)
)))
```

## 2. Declare the outcome and candidate features

Edit the positive and negative labels and the feature names. This simple guide
does not select features from the held-out data.

```{r}
positive_class <- "case"
negative_class <- "control"
predictors <- c("GENE_A", "GENE_B", "GENE_C")
threshold <- 0.5

stopifnot(all(c(positive_class, negative_class) %in% model_data$outcome))
stopifnot(all(predictors %in% names(model_data)))
stopifnot(all(stats::complete.cases(model_data[, predictors, drop = FALSE])))
stopifnot(all(c("train", "test") %in% model_data$split))
model_data$outcome <- factor(model_data$outcome,
                             levels = c(positive_class, negative_class))
train_data <- model_data |>
  dplyr::filter(split == "train") |>
  dplyr::select(sample_id, patient_id, outcome, dplyr::all_of(predictors))
test_data <- model_data |>
  dplyr::filter(split == "test") |>
  dplyr::select(sample_id, patient_id, outcome, dplyr::all_of(predictors))
test_predictors <- dplyr::select(test_data, dplyr::all_of(predictors))
stopifnot(nlevels(droplevels(train_data$outcome)) == 2)
stopifnot(nlevels(droplevels(test_data$outcome)) == 2)
```

## 3. Fit the model using training data only

The recipe estimates zero-variance filtering and scaling from the training
split. Bias reduction can stabilize logistic fits under separation; it does
not make a small cohort representative.

> **Training unit:** The model fits one row per sample. Patients with more
> samples therefore contribute more rows; grouping the split by patient
> prevents patient overlap but does not make fitting patient-level.

```{r}
recipe <- recipes::recipe(outcome ~ . - sample_id - patient_id, data = train_data) |>
  recipes::step_zv(recipes::all_predictors()) |>
  recipes::step_normalize(recipes::all_predictors())

model_spec <- parsnip::logistic_reg() |>
  parsnip::set_engine(
    "glm",
    family = stats::binomial(),
    method = brglm2::brglm_fit,
    type = "AS_mean"
  ) |>
  parsnip::set_mode("classification")

model_workflow <- workflows::workflow() |>
  workflows::add_recipe(recipe) |>
  workflows::add_model(model_spec)
model <- parsnip::fit(model_workflow, data = train_data)
```

## 4. Evaluate held-out patients with bootstrap uncertainty

The probability threshold is fixed above before evaluating the test set. If a
patient contributes several samples with the same outcome, this guide averages
their predicted probabilities so each patient contributes once. The bootstrap
resamples patients, not samples.

```{r}
probability <- predict(model, new_data = test_predictors, type = "prob")[[
  paste0(".pred_", positive_class)
]]
predicted_class <- factor(
  ifelse(probability >= threshold, positive_class, negative_class),
  levels = c(positive_class, negative_class)
)
predictions <- tibble::tibble(
  sample_id = test_data$sample_id,
  patient_id = test_data$patient_id,
  truth = test_data$outcome,
  probability = probability,
  predicted_class = predicted_class
)

patient_predictions <- predictions |>
  dplyr::group_by(patient_id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    truth = dplyr::first(truth),
    probability = mean(probability),
    sample_count = dplyr::n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    predicted_class = factor(
      ifelse(probability >= threshold, positive_class, negative_class),
      levels = c(positive_class, negative_class)
    )
  )
print(table(patient_predictions$truth))

roc_result <- yardstick::roc_auc(patient_predictions, truth, probability,
                                 event_level = "first")
pr_result <- yardstick::pr_auc(patient_predictions, truth, probability,
                               event_level = "first")
brier_score <- mean((as.integer(patient_predictions$truth == positive_class) -
                       patient_predictions$probability)^2)
confusion <- yardstick::conf_mat(patient_predictions, truth, predicted_class)
print(roc_result)
print(pr_result)
print(brier_score)
print(confusion)

set.seed(1234)
patient_bootstrap <- rsample::bootstraps(patient_predictions, times = 1000, strata = truth)
bootstrap_metrics <- purrr::map_dfr(patient_bootstrap$splits, function(split) {
  resampled <- rsample::analysis(split)
  tibble::tibble(
    roc_auc = yardstick::roc_auc(resampled, truth, probability,
                                 event_level = "first")$.estimate,
    pr_auc = yardstick::pr_auc(resampled, truth, probability,
                               event_level = "first")$.estimate,
    brier_score = mean((as.integer(resampled$truth == positive_class) -
                          resampled$probability)^2)
  )
})
metric_intervals <- tibble::tibble(
  metric = c("ROC AUC", "PR AUC", "Brier score"),
  lower_95 = c(
    stats::quantile(bootstrap_metrics$roc_auc, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
    stats::quantile(bootstrap_metrics$pr_auc, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
    stats::quantile(bootstrap_metrics$brier_score, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE)
  ),
  upper_95 = c(
    stats::quantile(bootstrap_metrics$roc_auc, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
    stats::quantile(bootstrap_metrics$pr_auc, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
    stats::quantile(bootstrap_metrics$brier_score, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
)
print(metric_intervals)

ggplot2::ggplot(patient_predictions, ggplot2::aes(x = truth, y = probability,
                                         color = predicted_class)) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(position = ggplot2::position_jitter(width = 0.1),
                      size = 2) +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = threshold, linetype = "dashed") +
  ggplot2::theme_bw() +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Observed class", y = "Predicted positive probability")
```

## 5. Save the model and held-out predictions

```{r}
dir.create("output", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
qs2::qs_save(model, "output/biomarker_model.qs2")
readr::write_tsv(predictions, "output/biomarker_test_predictions.tsv")
readr::write_tsv(patient_predictions, "output/biomarker_patient_test_predictions.tsv")
readr::write_tsv(roc_result, "output/biomarker_patient_roc_auc.tsv")
readr::write_tsv(pr_result, "output/biomarker_patient_pr_auc.tsv")
readr::write_tsv(tibble::tibble(brier_score = brier_score),
                 "output/biomarker_patient_brier_score.tsv")
readr::write_tsv(metric_intervals, "output/biomarker_patient_metric_intervals.tsv")
readr::write_tsv(as.data.frame(confusion$table), "output/biomarker_patient_confusion.tsv")
```

The patient-level bootstrap intervals are conditional on this fitted model and
split; they do not measure training or feature-selection instability. The
patient counts above matter: intervals from few patients per class are weak.
Brier score summarizes probability accuracy but is not a complete calibration
analysis. Cross-validation, threshold tuning, feature stability, and external
validation remain outside this compact guide; do not infer clinical performance
from one split.
